name: Shearlet Transform Analysis
description: Uses shearlet transform for multi-directional analysis — superior to wavelets for anisotropic features (Kutyniok et al., 2012).
mechanism:
This method applies the Shearlet Transform following Kutyniok & Labate (2012) for directional multi-scale forensic analysis:

1. **Shearlet System Construction**: A shearlet system is constructed using parabolic scaling matrices Aₐ = diag(a, √a) and shear matrices Sₛ. The shearlet ψₐ,ₛ,ₜ(x) = a⁻³/⁴ψ(Sₛ⁻¹Aₐ⁻¹(x−t)) provides near-optimal sparse representation of images with edges along curves.

2. **Directional Decomposition**: Unlike wavelets, shearlets capture directional information via the shear parameter, enabling anisotropic analysis across multiple orientations at each scale. This is particularly effective for detecting edge artifacts in AI-generated images that exhibit unnatural directional properties.

3. **Phase Congruency Analysis**: Shearlet-domain phase congruency measures the coherence of frequency components at edge locations. Natural edges show high phase congruency across scales, while AI-generated boundaries may show inconsistent phase relationships.

4. **Sparsity Profiling**: The shearlet representation sparsity (measured by ℓ¹/ℓ² ratio) is analyzed per block. Natural images achieve near-optimal sparsity in the shearlet domain due to the geometric regularity of natural edges. AI artifacts — ringing, grid patterns, texture discontinuities — reduce sparsity in characteristic ways.

5. **Edge Regularity Assessment**: The decay rate of shearlet coefficients across scales at detected edges is measured. Natural edges follow predictable decay patterns governed by Hölder regularity, while AI-generated edges often show anomalous coefficient decay indicating synthetic generation.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
